newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude market benefits from demand, U.S. arb.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude market benefits from demand, U.S. arb.

text.p: The North Sea market saw differentials move up amid good demand from both Europe and the United States after the transatlantic arbitrage window opened.

January Brent paper was untraded on the 15-day market but was valued in line with firmer front-month futures of $24 a barrel in morning business. Intermonth spreads were steady to firmer with Dec/Jan offered at +90 cents. Further forward spreads were unchanged with Jan/Feb at either side of 70 cents.
CFDs were expected to react to Wednesday's late Brent deal at Jan paper +49 cents. The only early deal heard was for the week of Dec 16-20 done at Jan +4, in line with closing levels.
"The market is firm. There is very good demand for everything," a wet trader said.
Gas oil-rich grade Oseberg finally saw its seasonal strength restored with a Dec 22-24 loading cargo selling at Dated Brent +47 cents late Wednesday, up nearly 10 cents from last traded.
Ekofisk too moved at steady levels with two cargoes loading end December bought by the same end-user for a number around Dated Brent +27/+28 though neither deal could be confirmed.
Sour Flotta was valued at a firmer Dated Brent -40 cents in view of continued tightness of Russian Urals, some of which moved into Northwest Europe earlier in the week.

"The market is very strong with some possible increases coming in coming days. The arb is open and there is good demand in the U.S. and Europe. The situation is rather healthy," a European trader said.
The Brent/WTI spread rose above a $1 on Thursday, lending credence to market talk of Brent barrels moving to the U.S.
The sole Brent cargo to turn wet on Wednesday was kept by a trading house and resold to a Wall Street trader at Jan Brent +49 cents, some five cents above Tuesday's highest traded level.
The buyer is thought to be holding at least three Brents already and is believed to be working a VLCC transatlantic.
